title: Shenmen NPC Role / Station (d100)
note: A generic role/station for any NPC in or passing through Shenmen — used to give an NPC a clearer job when the willowshore_resident table is too town-specific (travelers, off-map folk, officials, outsiders). Population skews human with kitsune, tengu, nagaji, halfling, elf, half-elf (aiuvarin), leshy and others. Pair with a name and an attitude from play. Keep Player != PC knowledge: no spoiler creatures named as a role.

entries.value: Farmer or rice/grain grower (Southbank tradition runs deep here)
Lumber worker or ex-lumber-camp hand (the trade that built the town, now waning)
Fisher or pond-keeper
Miller, baker, or grain-handler
Hunter, trapper, or forest ranger out of the hinterlands
Woodcarver, carpenter, or joiner
Smith, founder, or metalworker
Merchant or shopkeeper (general goods, dry goods, sundries)
Traveling peddler, tinker, or caravan trader (often Karahai-bound)
Innkeeper, cook, teahouse-keep, or tavern hand
Herbalist, apothecary, or alchemist
Doctor, healer, midwife, or bonesetter
Priest, shrine-keeper, or temple acolyte (Daikitsu, Pharasma, Abadar, Lady Nanbyo, others)
Wandering monk, pilgrim, or Sangpotshi practitioner walking the path
Fortune-teller, geomancer, or charm-seller (fulus, talismans, wards)
Town guard, watch officer, or ex-imperial soldier who stayed after the collapse
Appointed official, magistrate, clerk, or tax-collector (Lung Wa legacy)
Lawyer, scribe, calligrapher, or letter-writer
Scholar, tutor, librarian, or apprentice of an arcane tradition
Artist, actor, opera performer, musician, or storyteller
Boatwright, ferry-poler, dockhand, or riverboat pilot
Stablehand, drover, vet, or beast-keeper (the town avoids beef; cattle are working beasts)
Leatherworker, tanner, weaver, dyer, or papermaker
Distiller, brewer, vintner, or glassblower
Tea-farmer or tea merchant (leshy collectives are renowned for this)
Laborer, porter, or conscripted Industrial-District worker (a live grievance against the governor)
Beggar, drifter, orphan, or refugee from the empire's collapse
Smuggler, fence, or grower of illicit goods (drugs, poisons, contraband)
Bookmaker, gambler, or labor organizer
Retired elder, town historian, or keeper of oral lore
Caravan guard, sellsword, or bounty-hunter passing through
Bathhouse-keeper, barber, masseur, or tattooist
Inventor, gadgeteer, or engineer (dam, mills, machinery)
Foreign visitor or expatriate — Goka, Sze, Jinin, or further Tian Xia (on uncertain business)
Hidden power-broker or someone with quiet leverage over others (their station is a front)
